text:
I need to verify whether Pittsburgh was indeed named after a British Prime Minister.

Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania was named after William Pitt the Elder (also known as William Pitt, 1st Earl of Chatham), who served as British Prime Minister. The city was named in 1758 when General John Forbes captured the French Fort Duquesne and renamed it Fort Pitt in honor of William Pitt the Elder, who was Secretary of State at the time and effectively leading the British government during the Seven Years' War. The settlement that grew around the fort became known as Pittsburgh.

The other agents are correct in identifying Pittsburgh as the answer. This is a well-documented historical fact.

Answer: Pittsburgh
